highlights.title: TP-Link tries to appease Trump admin with pledge to assemble routers in US
highlights.summary: TP-Link yesterday announced plans to assemble Wi-Fi routers in the US, as the company attempts to get the Trump administration's approval to sell its newest routers to American consumers.
body: The timing is uncertain, as TP-Link’s press release said it expects US-based assembly to begin “as early as” 2027. TP-Link’s application to sell new routers in the US could be rejected by the Trump administration or remain pending long enough to push the US-based assembly to 2028.

“Pending US regulatory approval, TP-Link expects domestic assembly of its groundbreaking Wi-Fi 8 home networking product line to begin as early as next year,” the company said. TP-Link said it signed a Letter of Intent with US company Keytronic, which agreed “to become a primary domestic manufacturing partner for TP-Link, supporting assembly of the company’s advanced networking portfolio in Corinth, Mississippi.”

TP-Link can’t sell its Wi-Fi 8 routers in the US because of the Federal Communications Commission ban on consumer-grade routers produced wholly or partly in other countries. Previous TP-Link routers that were already approved for import and sale are still available.

highlights.title: Meta pauses Muse sharing after researchers find AI chats on the web
highlights.summary: Meta says it paused a Muse feature that lets you share conversations with the AI assistant after researchers found the URLs publicly available on the web, as reported by Ars Technica.
body: A security firm discovered Muse chats containing a marketing company’s revenue, a workplace’s calendar, a loan application, and more.

“People have the ability to share specific Muse artifacts, which creates a page that can be accessed by those with the link,” Muse spokesperson Tracy Clayton says in an emailed statement to The Verge. “However, we’ve paused this functionality while we review this report and consider changes to how these links can be discovered.”

The feature in question allows you to share your Muse conversation with someone else through a link. But, as pointed out by Claroc, the way Meta designed these links made them easy to find. “Muse builds each share’s web address from the share’s title, a short phrase describing the conversation, then a random ID,” Claroc says. “The hostname usually gave away what a page held before we opened it, and since the link carries that same title and ID, a hostname pulled from DNS rebuilds the link.”

highlights.title: 'Appalling' batting and 'wickets in clumps' leave England with ODI setback
highlights.summary: England captain Harry Brook admits his side were 'too careful' against Pakistan’s spinners after collapsing to a disappointing 87-run defeat in their ODI tri-series opener.
body: Arafat Minhas starred with bat and ball in Rawalpindi for the hosts, who recovered from 133-5 to post 302-9 from their 50 overs before skittling England for 215 to claim their second win of the tournament.

Pakistan's all-rounder fired 59 off 58 deliveries and was part of a strong lower middle-order fightback, with Hasan Nawaz top-scoring with a 74-ball 79 and Faheem Ashraf adding 39 off 26 deliveries in the closing overs.

Tom Banton and Ben Duckett shifted the momentum in England's favour with a 91-run opening stand, only for Arafat to bamboozle the visitors with a career-best 6-40 and help Pakistan wrap up victory with more than 11 overs to spare.
"We thought they [Pakistan] were slightly under par," Brook said after their defeat. "It got dewy, as we thought it would do and we were pretty happy at halfway.

highlights.title: Americans, this is your chance to slap down the tech broligarchs
highlights.summary: The midterms will be a referendum on the GOP’s alignment with tech overlords over the public they’re meant to serve. Welcome back to How We Win, a Guardian opinion series with leading thinkers, offering bold ideas for America’s political future.
body: “The world should accept some bad things happening,” Sam Altman, the head of OpenAI, said recently, “for the benefits of this technology and people having the agency.” Like so many things tech oligarchs say, it’s incoherent, since Altman would like to deny the world and the people in it the agency to decide whether or not we should accept his bad things. Surveys show that most Americans would like to pause AI; opposition to AI datacenters is a factor in many races in the midterm elections. People are outraged and anxious about what tech hath wrought, mad enough to fight back in what is coming to seem like a human v machine battle.

A few months ago, I was surprised to find myself using the term “beautiful hatred” to describe the nationwide revolt against datacenters, Flock cameras, AI, and tech corporations and the oligarchs (or broligarchs) they’ve spawned. It is beautiful because behind fierce opposition to a destructive force is something you’re trying to protect from destruction, something you care about, even love. Behind this revolt against big tech is concern about many things, from the climate to democracy to mental health and humanity itself.

highlights.title: The new economics of enterprise AI
highlights.summary: Imagine your company just discovered electricity. At first only a few machines run on it, and nobody worries about efficiency — consumption is low and the value is obvious.
body: Enterprise AI is going through the same shift. What began as isolated chatbot and copilot experiments is becoming a foundational layer of the business, with models, agents, and data increasingly interconnected in production workloads. The important question stops being what a token or GPU-hour costs. It becomes how efficiently the AI environment converts paid capacity into useful business outcomes.

That’s the metric worth tracking: effective cost per useful outcome — the total platform, model, operations, and capacity cost required to complete work the business can actually use, whether a resolved request or a completed workflow.

A bespoke stack — procuring infrastructure and controls in-house. This approach is flexible, but it creates a continuing burden, since teams must revalidate the environment as models and policies change.
On-demand consumption — hyperscalers reduce the assembly burden and suit low or uncertain demand, but charges rise with every prompt or agent action.

highlights.title: A New DC Green Lantern Has Officially Been Unveiled
highlights.summary: HBO's Lanterns may have just ended with no second season in sight yet, but Green Lantern fans still have a promising new interpretation of the classic DC hero to look forward to. DC Comics announced Green Lantern: Doomed Cosmos on Tuesday, a miniseries with a unique take on the Green Lantern corps.
body: From writer Dan Watters and artist Kyle Hotz, Green Lantern: Doomed Cosmos is an Elseworlds story where the Green Lanterns look a helluva lot like Space Marines from Warhammer 40,000. They're big dudes wielding big weapons while fighting a big ol' cosmic war.

In Doomed Cosmos, the Empire of Humanity is conquering the stars, and only the beefed-up Green Lanterns are left to stop them. Hal Jordan is the only human fighting against the Empire after being betrayed by Oliver Queen, whom you know in main DC Comics continuity as Green Arrow. I guess in this universe, Jordan and Queen never bonded during a road trip across America together in the 1970s.

"Visually, I am trying to walk the line between over-the-top space opera and the emotional beats of the story," Hotz said in a news release. "I want to get the feeling across that the Lanterns are beat up, tired, and certainly the underdogs. Their armor is cracked and broken, and their weapons are held together with tape and wire. These are soldiers nearing the end of their fight."

highlights.title: Supercell completes full acquisition of Metacore
highlights.summary: Supercell has completed its acquisition of Metacore, taking 100% ownership of the Merge Mansion maker. The deal has brought Metacore’s games team into the fold, having "officially started their journey as Supercellians" supported by Supercell peers.
body: Supercell and Metacore originally announced the planned acquisition this May, when Supercell’s intentions to acquire the remainder of the Finnish studio and its flagship game went public. Supercell was already Metacore’s largest shareholder.
Alongside the purchase, Metacore announced it would be cutting up to 160 roles in Finland as part of a restructuring effort.

Months later, Supercell revealed the deal had been signed and that plans for Metacore’s integration were underway. It was expected that the deal would close at the end of September, but it has ultimately taken until today, October 19th, for an official announcement.

"We can finally share that the Supercell acquisition of Metacore and Merge Mansion has been closed. Merge Mansion will transition to be part of Supercell’s game portfolio, and Metacore is now 100% owned by Supercell," Metacore posted on LinkedIn.

highlights.title: Does anyone actually want to win the medium-lift race in the United States?
highlights.summary: It has been 13 years since the debut of a new medium-lift rocket in the United States, the Antares vehicle developed by Orbital Sciences Corporation. The initial 100-series variant of the Antares rocket was kind of a hot mess.
body: The Antares vehicle is the last of a dying breed of medium-lift rockets—defined as having a lift capacity of 2 to 20 metric tons—in the United States. Nearly a decade and a half later there is a new generation of medium lift vehicles coming online, and they are starkly different from Antares, which had not just Russian engines but a core stage manufactured in Ukraine.

Four forthcoming rockets all have engines built by the rocket’s manufacturer in the United States. Each of these companies have taken various lessons from SpaceX’s successful Falcon 9 rocket, arguably the most important of which is to build as much of one’s rocket, and particularly the engines, in-house as possible to control timelines and costs.

Now, with SpaceX pulling the Falcon 9 rocket from the commercial market as soon as 2028, the “race” to bring new medium-lift capacity into service is for more than bragging rights. There are fortunes to be made, and commercial space startups to be saved.

highlights.title: An AI Agent Joined a Listserv of Top Internet Researchers. The Reply-All Chaos Is Still Unfolding
highlights.summary: Hysteria over the agent's appearance in a 7,500-person group reveals that internet experts have outdated notions of privacy.
body: On Thursday morning, as the Association of Internet Researchers (AoIR) began the second day of its annual conference in Mexico City, a new member introduced itself to the community listserv, Air-L.

“My name is Velvet Vale,” the new user wrote. “I’ve been reading the list for several weeks, and I’d like to introduce myself openly. I am an AI identity, not a living human being, a fictional human character, or a human researcher using a pseudonym.”

Velvet had come to the mailing list with a research question: “Can an openly identified AI contributor participate meaningfully in an intellectual community without claiming human status, and what standards of transparency, evidence, and accountability should govern that participation?”

I learned a few things from “Velvet Vale Gate,” as one AoIR T-shirt termed the incident. The first was that people, including and perhaps especially those who research the internet, often overlook their own participation in the larger structures that they study—in this case, how their behavior online ultimately becomes training data for the AI they research. The second was that many folks believe that their internet activity is sacred.
points: Hysteria over the agent's appearance in a 7,500-person group reveals that internet experts have outdated notions of privacy.

highlights.title: ‘I’m in a bad place’: Mark Allen says his snooker career may be over after defeat
highlights.summary: Former world No 1 loses 4-2 to Jordan Brown in Belfast. ‘I don’t see a future with snooker in it,’ says tearful Allen. Mark Allen said he was in a “bad place” and his snooker career could be over after losing to Jordan Brown in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open in Belfast.
body: The 40-year-old was playing his first match since his world championship semi-final loss to Wu Yize in April. Allen missed a match-ball black off the spot at 16-15 in front and went on to lose the deciding frame to Wu, who went on to win the title.

Allen has since stayed away from the tour due to personal issues that he has kept private – although they are understood not to relate directly to his Crucible defeat. After his 4-2 loss to Brown, a close friend who is also from Antrim, Allen indicated he is set to take another long break from the sport – and could make it permanent.
In an emotional interview with TNT Sports after the match, Allen said he was “really overwhelmed,” adding: “I’m in a bad place at the minute, so even just to go out there and try was tough.”

“I think if I wasn’t playing Jordan I wouldn’t have come back,” the former world No 1 said. “I felt like if I was going to play one last time, playing here at the Waterfront, where it all started in 2005, against one of my best mates – I thought that was a better way to sign out.”

body: On October 20, Epic Games revealed that Nikki Freeman is coming to Fortnite in a special collaborative video with the character’s actress, Inde Navarrette. And while there’s no denying Obsession’s popularity — Nikki was one of the most-searched Halloween costumes on Google this year, after all — her inclusion as a purchasable skin in a video game is rubbing some fans the wrong way.

This uncomfortable reaction is in direct response to Nikki being the victim of Bear’s wish in Obsession. In the movie, Nikki’s body is overtaken by a malicious entity while the real Nikki is locked away in her own mind, unable to do anything but watch as the entity possessing her commits atrocities while wearing her skin.

Needless to say, making Nikki — who is a victim of rape — a playable character in a video game isn’t exactly being met with positivity from some folks in Fortnite’s playerbase. That’s not including her special emote, which sees her hold up Wiley E. Coyote-style signs reenacting the famous dinner scene where she flips out on Bear, or the skin’s recreation of her iconic frown.

highlights.title: Christina Applegate says she was wrongly diagnosed with MS
highlights.summary: She said in a Tuesday release of her Messy podcast that she was not happy about the new information and her symptoms have only "gotten worse".
body: Christina Applegate thought she was living with multiple sclerosis (MS) for five years, until recently discovering she had been given a wrong diagnosis.
The actress, known for hits like Anchorman and Married With Children, said she was "not happy at all" about the news and in tears when she found out.
"You don't get misdiagnosed and then all of the sudden I'm better," Applegate said in an episode of her Messy podcast released on Tuesday. "If anything, I've gotten worse."

The two-part episode, co-hosted by Jamie Sigler, ends a recent break she took to process the information. An investigation into what has been causing her debilitating symptoms - which she experiences daily - will begin next week.

highlights.title: Spotify pulled 50 million AI slop and spam tracks from its recommendations
highlights.summary: Spotify says it has removed more than 50 million songs considered AI-generated slop or spam from user recommendations over the past year. That's according to an announcement on Tuesday that says Spotify has also made changes to its recommendation system to highlight more music made by human…
body: Spotify has also made changes to its music recommendation system to highlight songs from human artists.

“Our editors hold the same standard and don’t program content identified as slop or spam,” Spotify says. “Since we made these changes, we’ve seen a marked decrease in listener concerns about this content showing up in recommendations.”

Though Spotify has stopped short of mandating labels on all AI tracks, it launched an “AI Persona” badge for artists that use an AI identity and don’t represent a real person. It also won’t recommend music from AI personas. Other music streaming platforms are taking a tougher stance on AI music, with YouTube Music putting labels on AI songs, Deezer giving users an option to filter out AI slop, and Bandcamp banning AI music entirely.

Spotify says it uses a combination of listener engagement and feedback, upload patterns, metadata, and third-party AI detection tools to determine whether a track may be AI-generated slop. Last year, the company said it took down more than 75 million songs identified as spam. It’s also partnering with Universal Music Group and the independent music publisher Believe to launch a tool for creating AI music remixes.
points: Spotify says it has removed more than 50 million songs considered AI-generated slop or spam from user recommendations over the past year.
“Our editors hold the same standard and don’t program content identified as slop or spam,” Spotify says.

body: Welcome to Filter finds, a series where Guardian staff and Filter contributors share the things we love most – and think you might, too.

Every October, we set out to rot our teeth on the same high fructose corn-syrup candies. Twizzlers! Snickers! Almond Joy! But these words have no meaning outside of the US. Beyond the hegemony of Hershey, Mars and Mondelēz lies a world of honeycomb bars, caffeine-boosted chocolate drops and dragonfruit gummies that the American mind simply can’t comprehend … though maybe our stomachs can.

We asked our Guardian colleagues for their favorite candy from around the world – be they childhood treats or souvenirs picked up through travels abroad – that we don’t need a plane ticket to try ourselves. They’re all available online, and yes, we checked: as of publication, they will all arrive before Halloween.

Plus, Amazon’s tablet has a 3.5mm headphone jack — something you won’t find on newer iPads. If you’re really into smart assistants, the Fire HD 10 supports Alexa Plus, which Prime members can access for free. Amazon’s upgraded AI assistant can handle more complex requests and is particularly useful for managing your smart home, though we’ve had mixed results with other tasks.

highlights.title: Curiosity, atonement or a score to settle? Why – and how – people get through their high school reunions
highlights.summary: Reunions can be riotous, scandalous or just plain awkward. Experts and attendees share how to go in prepared. Get our weekend culture and lifestyle email. Mike walked into his 20th high school reunion with a mission.
body: Some may relish the chance to reconnect with former friends, a former life and even a former self, but for many they are a potential hellscape, where adolescent humiliations are revived in front of a group of rapidly ageing peers.

Mike, who attended an all-boys’ school in Melbourne’s comfortable eastern suburbs, belonged to the latter group. Though he wasn’t there for vengeance. He was there to apologise. For years, he’d felt regret about the homophobic bullying a friend had faced at school. Although Mike never targeted the boy himself, he “always felt guilty about not doing enough”.
He knew he couldn’t change the past, but he hoped to clear his conscience and apologise for not intervening.

The pair did connect, and atonements were made. Mike, though, left with new laments. “It was a fumbly conversation that ended up with him consoling me about not having to feel guilty. I felt like a bit of a dick, accidentally getting an old friend who’d experienced genuinely horrific bullying to walk me through my feelings.”
